title: Config-aware tool routing & argument-validation eval harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated, config-aware evaluation harness that detects quality regressions in tool/function calling due to model version changes, runtime config flips (e.g., tokenization, kv-cache policies, quantization profile), and routing policy updates. This harness focuses on two core dimensions: 1) tool selection accuracy (the model chooses the correct tool/endpoint for a given prompt), and 2) argument validation & sanitization (arguments conform to the tool schema and are robust to prompt noise).

Scope:
- Offline datasets: curated customer prompt replay subset, synthetic adversarial prompts, and edge-case generator.
- Metrics: tool selection accuracy, top-K tool coverage, false-invoke rate (calls to incorrect tools), argument-schema pass rate, sanitization repair rate, and per-tool latency impact.
- Integrations: run on PRs that change model pinning, approved runtime config files, and routing policy YAMLs. Results publish to the evals dashboard with trendlines and automatic regression alerts.
- CI gating: canary threshold for auto-blocking of model/config rollouts if key metrics degrade beyond configured SLO deltas.

Why this work: Past incidents showed subtle behavioral shifts when we updated a tokenization patch and when swapping to a quantized model variant; these caused incorrect tool selections and malformed args that silently failed downstream. This harness aims to catch those regressions earlier in the release pipeline and provide actionable diffs (per-example telemetry) for model/runtime engineers.

Design highlights / approach:
- Config-aware baseline: every run compares a candidate set (new model/config) against a stable baseline; diffs surface both selection and argument-level deltas.
- Golden datasets: label each prompt with expected tool and canonical argument schema. Use a mix of human-labeled customer examples and synthetic edge cases generated with mutation operators (e.g., truncation, punctuation swaps, injection patterns).
- Error injection: intentionally scramble args and add noise to verify sanitizers and schema enforcement in the runtime.
- Scoring: weight metrics by customer frequency and business-critical tools; produce a single composite regression score plus per-tool breakdown.
- Explainability: include per-example traces (prompt, model output, parsed args, validation errors) and small diffs highlighting changed tokens or parse trees.
- Deployment: library + runner in evals infra, a Dockerized task for CI, and a lightweight dashboard panel with baseline/candidate comparisons and time series.

Trade-offs considered:
- Cost vs coverage: full replay of customer traffic is expensive; we sample a stratified subset focusing on high-impact customers and tools.
- Strict gating vs velocity: initially will surface regressions and require manual review; later we will tune to auto-block only high-confidence regressions for P0 tools.
- False positives from ambiguous prompts: we will include an uncertainty bucket and human-in-the-loop review for ambiguous examples before gating.

Deliverables:
- Runner that accepts baseline/candidate configurations and outputs metric diffs (JSON + human report).
- Labeled datasets & mutation scripts stored in evals-infra repo.
- CI integration that runs on targeted PRs and scheduled nightly sweeps.
- Dashboard panels + alerting rules in Datadog/Grafana for trend detection.

Operational notes:
- Baseline selection: default to release pinned model; allow manual override to any historical snapshot.
- Thresholds: initial thresholds will be conservative (5% relative drop in argument-schema pass rate or 3% absolute drop in tool selection accuracy triggers alert).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can compare candidate vs baseline and emit per-tool metric diffs within 30 minutes for the standard test set.
Detects injected argument-schema violations with >95% recall on synthetic tests.
CI integration: PRs that change model pinning or routing YAMLs trigger the harness and post results as an artifact in the PR.
Dashboard shows baseline vs candidate trends and alerting rules send to #eval-regressions when thresholds are breached.
Documentation and runbook for oncall engineers describing triage steps and rollback guidance.
